legacy_root.question: What does a router regression suite look like elsewhere (golden query sets, drift alarms, coverage of never-selected capabilities), and how do they detect the specific failure where a capability exists but is never selected?
legacy_root.title: Extract how other systems build a regression suite that proves a router still routes

claims.claim: Elsewhere, a router/ranker regression suite is a labeled golden query set: typical queries plus per-query document (or item) ratings, scored by a ranking metric. OpenSearch/_rank_eval is the structured form of that pattern.
claims.strongest_caveat: rank_eval is search ranking, not LLM tool routing. The transferable mechanism is the labeled (query, relevant-id) set, not Elasticsearch/OpenSearch as a runtime.

rails.quoted_span: Allows to evaluate the quality of ranked search results over a set of typical search queries
The Rank Evaluation API evaluates the quality of ranked search results.

claims.claim: LlamaIndex RouterQueryEngine selects one of several candidate query engines from tool metadata/descriptions. The router itself has no check that a registered candidate is ever chosen.
claims.strongest_caveat: Absence of a never-selected check in this module is not proof that no LlamaIndex user has one in their own eval harness.

rails.quoted_span: Selects one out of several candidate query engines to execute a query.
Routers are modules that take in a user query and a set of “choices” (defined by metadata), and returns one or more selected choices.

claims.claim: Function-calling eval suites (BFCL) use labeled (query, expected function) cases plus a relevance/irrelevance class for when a function should not be invoked. That class is the false-alarm cousin of never-selected: it tests SHOULD-never-call, not exists-but-never-called.
claims.strongest_caveat: BFCL scores whether the model matches the labeled function on cases that exist in the dataset. A catalog function that never appears as a gold label is invisible to the leaderboard score.

rails.quoted_span: first comprehensive and executable function call evaluation
when the provided function is not suitable

claims.claim: NLU/intent evaluation only reports labels that appear in the test examples. Rasa evaluate_intents drops examples with no intent target and builds the label set from unique_labels of targets and predictions, so an intent that is never a target and never predicted does not show up as a failure. Rasa Pro E2E coverage metrics separately flag untested flows.
claims.strongest_caveat: The OSS evaluate_intents mechanism and the Pro E2E coverage docs are the same *pattern* on two products, not one binary. unique_labels would also hide a capability that the model never predicts if it is also absent from y_true.

rails.quoted_span: Only considers those examples with a set intent. Others are filtered out.
Coverage metrics help you see which flows and commands are not tested.

claims.claim: Unleash detects unused-looking flags by marking them potentially stale after expected lifetime, and allows a manual stale mark after the flag has served its purpose without tearing down the live configuration. Time-based unused is an analog of never-selected, not a router gold-set join.
claims.strongest_caveat: Potentially-stale is lifetime, not 'never chosen for a labeled query'. Kill-switches and rollback flags that remain configured but unused are the false-alarm case if unused==defect.

rails.quoted_span: async updatePotentiallyStaleFeatures
You can also manually mark a feature flag as stale if you know it has served its intended purpose.

claims.claim: Haystack ConditionalRouter documents an explicit fallback route when no specified condition matches. That is the no-capability-fits path, complementary to never-selected: empty gold expected-set queries must not be forced onto a catalog item.
claims.strongest_caveat: A fallback route does not detect a registered route that is never taken; it only handles unmatched conditions.

rails.quoted_span: Example usage with a default fallback route in a Pipeline:
fallback route

claims.claim: LangSmith documents offline evaluation on curated datasets and online evaluation on production traces to catch regressions.
claims.strongest_caveat: Single prose rail only (no independent structured API capture of LangSmith). Graded E3; must not be cited as measured fact.

rails.quoted_span: catch regressions

claims.claim: Public router suites already ship a first-class detector named for the failure 'a capability exists in the catalog but is never selected'.
claims.strongest_caveat: The fetched suites provide adjacent mechanisms (golden ratings, unique_labels gaps, stale flags, irrelevance cases, fallback routes) but none of the captured sources specify the catalog+gold+selection-log join as a named check. The detector below is a synthesis, not a copy of one upstream file.

rails.quoted_span: Selects one out of several candidate query engines to execute a query.
function relevance detection

never_selected_detector.title: never-selected capability detector

data_source.selection_log: the log produced by running the golden query set through the router (CI), or a production trace window with the same schema (query_id, selected_capability_ids)

when_it_runs: CI: immediately after the router regression suite writes a selection log for the golden query set
periodic: over a production selection-log window using the same join (optional second rail; not required to fire in CI)
never_selected_detector.algorithm: never_selected_routing_defect = (gold expected ids ∩ catalog selectable ids) − selected ids. corpus_gap = selectable ids − gold expected ids (untested, not a routing defect). never_by_design (selectable=false) is excluded from both.

false_alarm_case.why_it_should_never_be_selected: Admin kill-switch / dump path catalogued for operators. A user-task golden set must not treat 'never selected' as a defect for this id. deprecated.rollback_only is the same class.
false_alarm_case.naive_detector_that_false_alarms: catalog_ids − selected_ids with no selectable filter
